title: Guillain–Barre syndrome in acute lymphoblastic leukemia: Causal or coincidental
case_prompt: A 10-year-old boy with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed 3 months earlier (bone marrow: 95% precursor B-ALL; CSF without blasts) is receiving induction chemotherapy per MRC UK ALL-12 protocol (daunorubicin and vincristine on days 1, 8, 15, and 22; prednisolone days 1–28; L-asparaginase days 17–28). During the fourth week of therapy, three days after his fourth dose of vincristine, he developed rapidly progressive ascending weakness of all four limbs over 48 hours without any preceding infection. On examination, he had pure motor areflexic quadriplegia (upper-limb power grade 3, lower-limb grade 0) with intact bladder, respiratory, and bulbar functions. Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis (14 300/mm^3) and thrombocytopenia (98 700/mm^3). CSF analysis revealed glucose 53 mg/dL, protein 128 mg/dL, 5 lymphocytes/mm^3, and no blasts. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and spine was normal. On day 5 of illness, electrophysiological evaluation demonstrated a pure motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy: bilateral peroneal and tibial nerves were unexcitable; median and ulnar nerves had reduced compound muscle action potentials, prolonged latencies, and normal conduction velocities; F waves were absent in the lower limbs and prolonged in the upper limbs; sensory nerve action potentials were normal; needle electromyography showed a neurogenic pattern.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Vincristine-induced neuropathy — “Vincristine induced neuropathy, is a toxic, ‘dying-back’ neuropathy with prominent sensory involvement.”
2. Hereditary neuropathy unmasking — “Neither was there any finding on examination nor any family history suggestive of a hereditary neuropathy.”
3. Carcinomatous infiltration — “CSF showed glucose - 53 mg/dL; protein - 128 mg/dL; cell count - 5 lymphocytes/mm^3 and absent blasts cells. Contrast enhancing magnetic resonance imaging spine and brain, anti-nuclear antibody and rest were normal.”
4. Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP) — “Electrophysiological evaluation done on day 5 of illness revealed a pure motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy pattern.”
5. Acute motor axonal neuropathy variant of GBS — “Correlating the clinical and electrophysiological findings, acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN) – a subtype of GBS was kept.”
